Kettle Street brings British life sim chaos to Android, complete with nosy neighbours and butties
articles.summary: Three years of living in the UK has prepared me for a worrying amount of Kettle Street. It’s a cosy British life sim out now on Android. Its furniture shop even leaves your deliveries with a neighbour as a matter of course, which is the most realistic thing I’ve seen in a life sim. You’ve just moved into a bare flat in a small town called Kettleby. Maureen at number 11 has already put the kettle on. From there it’s about finding work, paying your way and turning the place into a home one wage packet at a time. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: Mika: Dungeon Backpacker makes you pack the heroes’ bags before sending them into danger
articles.summary: If I’m playing a game called Mika: Dungeon Backpacker, I’d expect her to be the hero of her own story. Except she really isn’t. She’s a Dungeon Supporter, which as far as I can tell means she packs everyone’s bags while four heroes take the credit. It’s a backpack-building roguelite with grid-based dungeons, and it’s coming soon to iOS and Android. The setting is Stonia, a continent that’s slowly turning into dungeons, and Mika’s latest job takes her into the ruins of a cathedral where an expedition disappeared a century ago. Something has been asleep down there ever since. Cheerful stuff. ... [ MORE ]

Legends of Amberland II brings its 90s-inspired RPG adventure to iOS and Android soon
articles.summary: If you played Legends of Amberland on PC, you probably waited four years for a sequel. On phones, you’ll be waiting about eleven days. Legends of Amberland II: The Song of Trees is coming to iOS and Android, hot on the heels of the first game’s mobile release back in August. It’s another first-person, turn-based dungeon crawler built on 90s PC role-playing, so you’re moving square by square, turning in neat 90-degree steps, with a party of up to seven heroes. You can hand-pick their classes and races or take a pre-made group if you’d like to get going. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: Training Hero Remastered rebuilds its engine without wiping your hard-earned progress
articles.summary: Training Hero is just like Mr Miyagi. No shortcuts, just push-ups until you’ve earned the right to hit someone. Which makes it a bit rich that it’s just had a full engine transplant. Daerisoft has now rebuilt the whole thing in Unity, and Training Hero Remastered is out now on iOS and Android, with the training record you’ve spent years building carried across. As for why, the original hasn’t had much new in it for a while. Its last proper content drop arrived in January 2022, and almost everything since has been bug fixes. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: The Captain - Pocket Edition finally brings its sci-fi adventure to iOS and Android
articles.summary: The Captain has taken its time getting to your phone. Indie Fund put money behind it back in 2017, it didn’t reach PC until 2021, and Switch got it a year after that. Now it’s out on iOS and Android as The Captain - Pocket Edition. It’s a pixel-art point-and-click from Sysiac Games, which is Peter Hedin and Benny Eriksson, two Swedes who’ve been making games together since they were kids. Tomorrow Corporation, of Little Inferno and Human Resource Machine fame, is publishing. ... [ MORE ]

articles.title: Dunk City Dynasty adds Manu Ginóbili and Lauri Markkanen for Season 10
articles.summary: Manu Ginobili made his name coming off the bench, so it’s a little funny seeing him lead anything. He heads up Season 10 Part 1 in Dunk City Dynasty, out now on iOS and Android, with Finnish All-Star Lauri Markkanen alongside him. If you haven’t been keeping up, this is NetEase’s NBA-licensed 3v3 streetball game, and it brings in a couple of new names most seasons. Season 9 opened with Anthony Edwards and Mikal Bridges. articles.title: Abelina is a strange, platforming romp through a natural afterlife from a former League of Legends animator and the composer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil
articles.summary: I have no particular thoughts on what the afterlife may look like, namely because if there is one, and I'm allowed to hang out in it, I don't want to be disappointed. What if I have the expectation that it's a hedonistic paradise and am met with only having a guy named Gary who only eats cheese sandwiches for company? How embarrassing! No, I'll leave the imagining to others on this particular front. Doing so bears some ripe fruit for me occasionally, too, as is the case today with Abelina, a surreal platformer about a man who died and finds himself tending to gardens and carving masks and trying "not to think about what this place might really be." Read more
